files: open, pathlib and os raise PermissionError

kernel.blocked_job: a job that cannot start (held, queue paused) is an error, not an endless wait
kernel.check: type-checks in a copy of the session; what the part of the script before its first command raises at run time (it has no params) is not an error of the check
kernel.destructive_commands: project_new, project_load, project_open, store_open and remove_*: RuntimeError unless the run allows them; `nyx run` allows them

futures.pending_at_end: the job of a future left pending when a script ends is cancelled

kernel.guard_limit_kernel: the traced-function guard reads one script: a function defined by an earlier script and given as a formula in a later one is not seen
kernel.params: the dict given to the run, bound in the script as `params` (an empty dict when none)
kernel.session: one Monty session outlives a script: variables, functions and imports stay from one script to the next; the static check knows them
kernel.waiting_rule: started without waiting, then polled by the host; when the caller's time is spent the script stays paused at the call and the run answers `running`; the value is the value of the blocking call; the polling is not a script command
kernel.worker_loss: a worker that dies is replaced and restored from the dump taken after the last script that finished

language: Python syntax, run by Monty 1.6.0 in a worker process (no CPython)

limits.seconds_counts: script time only; the time the engine takes to answer a command is not counted

output: print() lines, up to the output limit

path_guard.root: the workspace given to the run, else the folder of the script; relative paths are taken from it

static_check: names and required-ness of commands and arguments, against the stub of nyx api stubs; value types are not checked

traced_function.branch_rule: if, while, a if c else b, and, or, not, assert, a comparison, math.f and min/max on a value that depends on the point are refused before the script runs, with the line; write where(cond, a, b)
traced_function.called: once per command, with a symbolic point; the text it builds is the engine formula of the same words (parsed by femcore::formula)
traced_function.form: nyx.<command>(expr=f, ...) with f a def or a lambda of one argument, the point p; also trace(f) for its text
traced_function.guard_limit: syntactic: a value the guard cannot follow (a function chosen at run time) is not seen, and then `if sym:` takes the true branch
traced_function.numbers: written with repr: finite int or float; an integer stays an integer
traced_function.point: p["E"] (a vector, with .x .y .z), p["eps_r"], p["Ex"], p["nx"]: a name of a formula; p.x p.y p.z the coordinates

value: the last expression of the script, as JSON
